html:
The Mosque of Fakhr ad-Din stands in the old Hamar Weyne quarter of Mogadishu, Somalia. An inscription dates it to 1269, which makes it one of the oldest dated mosques on the East African coast.

It is named after Fakhr ad-Din, whom tradition makes the first ruler of the Sultanate of Mogadishu. The town was then a rich port, trading gold, ivory and cloth across the Indian Ocean, linked with the Swahili towns further south and with Arabia and Persia. The mosque is built of coral stone and marble. When Ibn Battuta visited Mogadishu in 1331, he found a wealthy Muslim city with its own sultan and judges.
